Article.ArticleTitle: Long-term variation of the macrobenthic community and its relationship with environmental factors in the Yangtze River estuary and its adjacent area.

Abstract.AbstractText: Using data from four periods from 1959 to 2015, we report the long-term variation of the macrobenthic community in the Yangtze River estuary and its adjacent area. In total, 624 species were collected, and Polychaeta was the dominant group. Significant differences between the four periods were found. The CCA (canonical correspondence analysis) and RDA (redundancy analysis) results revealed that temperature, salinity, and depth significantly influenced the macrobenthic communities (89.6% of the species-environment relationship variance was explained by the first two axes of CCA and 94.3% was explained by RDA). The results of K-dominance curves (the elevation increased over time), ABC (abundance/biomass comparison) curves (the W value changed from 0.311 to 0.167 during 1959 to 2014-2015) and the Shannon-Wiener index (log base=2; 2.29-5.03 in 1959, 2.86-4.55 in 2000-2001, 2.28-4.56 in 2011-2012, and 1.79-4.43 in 2014-2015) showed that the ecological status of the benthic study area was deteriorating.
